tool.name: hubCheck
tool.command: ## ⛔ NOT "aggressive", AND IT WAS. Aggressive mode scans the job's stdout/stderr for error ## text -- but both streams are redirected into the report dataset below, so there was ## nothing left to scan and it silently degraded to exit_code anyway. Declaring it claimed a ## check that could not run. hubCheck's exit status is meaningful and authoritative here. ## ## ⚠ THE REPORT IS THE DIAGNOSIS, so it is copied to stderr as well. Previously a hub defect ## failed the job and the only copy of the reason sat in a dataset marked error, with the ## job's stderr empty -- nothing to read in the invocation view. No process substitution: ## the job script is not guaranteed to run under bash (see faToTwoBit's note). ## ## ⛔ THE FLAG LIVES IN `truevalue`, NOT IN AN `#if`, SO THIS TOOL CAN BECOME A UDT. A ## User-Defined Tool carries a `shell_command`, where a leading `#` is a SHELL COMMENT -- so ## `udt_convert.py` refuses any wrapper whose command holds a Cheetah directive rather than ## translate it and silently drop the branch. `#if str($settings_level) -settings #end if` was ## that blocker and was the ONLY one here: hubCheck needs a single package, unlike faToTwoBit and ## bedToBigBed, which each need two and so cannot have one container at all. ## ## ⚠ The rendered command is unchanged in both states. A boolean's `falsevalue=""` emits nothing, ## and putting the flag in `truevalue` is where Galaxy expects it -- the `#if` was only ever ## re-deriving what the boolean already knew. Both <test>s still assert both sides. hubCheck $no_tracks $settings_level '$hub_url' > '$report' 2>&1 ; rc=\$? ; cat '$report' >&2 ; exit \$rc

param.label: Hub URL
param.help: URL (or local path) of the hub.txt to validate.

param.name: no_tracks
param.label: Skip per-track data checks
param.help: Check hub/genome/track structure only; do not fetch and validate track data files.

param.name: settings_level
param.label: Report setting support level
param.help: Output the support level of each track setting encountered.

tool.help:
**hubCheck** — validate the structure and settings of a UCSC **track hub**.
hubCheck walks a hub starting from its `hub.txt`, follows `genomes.txt` and each `trackDb`, and reports problems: missing required settings, unreadable `bigDataUrl` targets, malformed track stanzas, unsupported settings, etc. It is the standard pre-flight check before publishing a hub.
-----
**Input**
- `Hub URL` — URL (or path) of the top-level `hub.txt`.
**Output**
- A plain-text validation report. A clean hub yields no warnings.
-----
**Key options**
- `-noTracks` — validate hub/genome/trackDb structure only, skipping fetch and validation of the underlying track data files (faster, works offline-ish). - `-settings` — annotate each track setting with its support level.
**Note**
A meaningful end-to-end check requires a complete, fetchable hub (hub.txt, genomes.txt, a 2bit assembly, and all bigDataUrl targets). The bundled test only exercises that the executable is invocable and fails on a missing hub.
-----
**References**
- UCSC track hub reference: https://genome.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/help/hgTrackHubHelp.html - `hubCheck` source: https://github.com/ucscGenomeBrowser/kent/blob/master/src/hg/utils/hubCheck/hubCheck.c - Pre-built binaries and the full usage text: https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/admin/exe/linux.x86_64/FOOTER.txt
